# Focus-trapped modal

A dialog that keeps focus inside while it is open, closes with Esc, and hands focus back to whatever opened it. Built on the native `<dialog>` element.

## Use when

A short task must be finished or dismissed before going back: confirming a delete, a two-field form, a quick setting.

## Avoid when

Long forms, content people want to compare with the page, or anything that could be its own page or an inline message. Every modal interrupts.

## Drop it in

Copy the `Modal/` folder (`Modal.tsx`, `Modal.css`, `index.ts`).

```tsx
import { Modal } from './components/Modal';

const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);

<button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Rename</button>
<Modal open={open} onClose={() => setOpen(false)} title="Rename file" description="Up to 40 characters.">
  <form onSubmit={save}>…</form>
</Modal>
```

Props: `open`, `onClose` (Esc, backdrop click, your own buttons), `title` (its accessible name), `description`, `initialFocusRef`, `closeOnBackdrop` (default true), `size` (`small` or `medium`), `hideTitle`.

Theme with `--modal-bg`, `--modal-text`, `--modal-muted`, `--modal-border`, `--modal-radius`, `--modal-backdrop`, `--modal-font`.

## Design notes

- Give it a clear title and one primary action. Put Cancel first, so the safe choice is easy.
- Keep it short. If it scrolls, it probably wants to be a page.
- Turn off backdrop closing when a stray click would lose typed work.

## Accessibility

- `showModal()` makes the rest of the page inert, so screen readers and clicks stay inside. Tab and Shift+Tab wrap around inside the dialog instead of escaping to the browser toolbar. See [[native-dialog]].
- Focus moves in on open (the first field, or `initialFocusRef`) and back to the opener on close. For a destructive confirm, focus Cancel. See [[focus-management]].
- Esc always closes it. That is the way out that keeps it from being a keyboard trap (WCAG 2.1.2). See [[keyboard-navigation]].
- The title is the dialog's accessible name (`aria-labelledby`), and the description is linked with `aria-describedby`.
- Reduced motion: no fade or rise, it simply appears. See [[reduced-motion]].
